items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend chapter 1017 of the laws of 1963 relating to establishing the
Uniondale public library district in the town of Hempstead, Nassau county, in
relation to certain dates pertaining to the annual election process and
certain rights of the board
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4818

SPONSOR: THOMAS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend chapter 1017 of the laws of 1963 relating to establish-
ing the Uniondale public library district in the town of Hempstead,
Nassau county, in relation to certain dates pertaining to the annual
election process and certain rights of the board

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To amend outdated provisions related to Uniondale public library's
election process and rights of the board.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill changes the date for annual elections for
district Trustee, changes the date of publication of notice of the
election, clarifies the District Board's right to provide by resolution,
that such nominations be submitted in petition form subscribed by twen-
ty-five qualified voters of the district, clarify the District Board's
right to provide, by resolution, for absentee ballots, correct the hours
of polling and the fees for poll workers, clarify the District Board's
right to designate alternative inspectors and clerical help, and removes
the requirement of land ownership as a prerequisite to holding public
office as a Trustee.

Section two is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill amends Section 3 of the Special Act, which created the library
district, to alter certain date pertaining to the annual election proc-
ess and to clarify certain rights of the board. These amendments will
provide additional time for the public to participate in the electoral
process.

This bill corrects and clarifies certain procedural aspects of the
District's annual election for District Trustee. The Special Act, as
amended by Chapter 779 of the Laws of 1964, modeled the mechanics of
holding annual elections to that of fire districts and borrowed several
provisions from the Section 175 and Section 176 of the Town Law, as it
existed at such time. However, since then, Section 175 of the Town law
has been amended to provide for a longer procedural timeframe for the
mechanics of holding annual elections, but the Special Act was not simi-
larly amended.

The current versions of Sections 175 and Section 176 of the Town Law
provide for a publication of not less than 27 nor more than 34 days
prior to the election and provide that fire district commissioners may
require nominating petitions be subscribed by at least 25 residents and
be submitted 20 days prior to the election. In addition, provisions
related to special district elections have different procedural time-
frames than fire district elections date of publication at least 20 days
before the date of the election under Town Law § 212 and nominating
petitions due at least 30 days before the election pursuant to Town Law
§ 215). This bill amends Section 3 of the Special Act to expand the

election timeline, as it was expanded for fire districts. This amendment
will allow for greater participation by the electorate.

In addition, this bill changes the date of the annual election to a date
in October. Currently, the Special Act sets the date of annual election
on the first Tuesday of December. Historically, it has proven difficult
for the electorate to appear in person to vote at the annual election
due mainly to weather conditions and less daylight in December. As such,
an election date of the third Thursday in October will generally allevi-
ate weather conditions, occur prior to daylight savings and therefore
provide for greater voter turnout.

This bill changes the hours of polling to be consistent with fire
district and special district elections, i.e. between the hours of six
o'clock in the evening until nine o'clock in the evening and such addi-
tional consecutive hours prior thereto as the trustees may determine.
This amendment provides for the same voting hours as special district
elections under Town Law § 212 and for fire district elections under
Town Law § 175.

In addition, it raises the amount of compensation for election inspec-
tors and clerks, which was originally set in the Special Act at a maxi-
mum of ten dollars. It also clarifies the Board's right to designate
additional alternative inspectors who shall assume the office of inspec-
tor upon the inability or refusal of an inspector to assume or perform
his/her duties and to designate additional clerical help as needed.

Finally, this bill removes the Special Act's requirement imposing land
ownership as a prerequisite to holding office as a Trustee. The Special
Act's requirement of land ownership has been held unconstitutional.
Specifically, both federal and state courts have held that the equal
protection and due process clauses forbid the State from imposing land
ownership as a prerequisite to holding public office (see, Landes v Town
of N. Hempstead, 20 NY2d 417  
1967). Accordingly, the bill corrects
this provision and removes the Special Act's imposition of land owner-
ship as a condition to holding office as a Trustee.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New legislation.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
